how_to_inline: Paste lib/min/<name>.js files (field `min_file`) verbatim, one after another, into a single <script type="module"> in index.html, then write the piece below them. Each min file is the raw lib/<name>.js with comments and whitespace stripped and local variables shortened; every top-level name (exports and reserved) keeps its raw spelling, and each file ends in one `export{...}` list, which is legal in an inline module script. Files have no imports between them. Do not redeclare any name listed in a file's exports or reserved list. Budgets count the bytes you paste: `min_bytes` for lib/min, `raw_bytes` for lib/ (read lib/<name>.js for the commented source).
constraint_night: constraint-night in `compos` means only the variants listed in a file's `constraint_night`. No lib file fits 1kb-micro (copy a GLSL snippet instead) or css-only (no JS rendering); no-canvas allows only the pure JS maths (noise, 2D sdf, palette, easing) driving SVG or DOM.
glsl: Every GLSL snippet targets #version 300 es under webgl2.js GL_HEAD (precision highp float, highp int, highp sampler2D; uniforms u_time, u_reduced, u_res, u_mouse, u_audio; output `o`). Pick snippets with noiseGlsl(...) and sdfGlsl(...), which add dependencies once, in order. If you write your own header, keep `precision highp int;` because the hashes use uint.
4k_shader: No whole file fits a 4K intro. Copy only the GLSL snippet strings you need (sizes in glsl_bytes) plus a hand-written 10-line bootstrap modelled on webgl2.js glStart.

exports.name: mulberry32
exports.summary: mulberry32(seed) -> () => float in [0, 1). Fast seeded PRNG; use it everywhere a piece needs randomness.

exports.name: xoshiro128ss
exports.summary: xoshiro128ss(a, b, c, d) -> () => float in [0, 1). Longer-period PRNG from four 32-bit seeds (not all zero).

exports.name: simplex
exports.summary: simplex(seed) -> { n2(x, y), n3(x, y, z) }, seeded gradient noise in [-1, 1]; n2(0, 0) is 0.

exports.name: fbm
exports.summary: fbm(n, oct = 5, lac = 2, gain = 0.5) -> (x, y, z) => sum with |sum| < 1. Pass n2 or n3.

exports.name: ridged
exports.summary: ridged(n, oct, lac, gain) -> (x, y, z) => [0, 1). Ridged multifractal: crests, veins, mountain spines.

exports.name: warp
exports.summary: warp(f, k = 1) -> (x, y) => f(p + k * (f(p + o1), f(p + o2))). Quilez domain warp of any 2D field.

exports.name: NOISE_GLSL
exports.summary: GLSL snippets name -> [deps, code]: hashU (uint mix), hash31 (vec3 -> [0, 1)), hash33 (vec3 -> [-1, 1]^3), vnoise (vec2 value noise [0, 1]), gnoise (vec3 quintic gradient noise ~[-1, 1]), fbm, ridged, warp (3 fbm calls: expensive on SwiftShader).

exports.name: noiseGlsl
exports.summary: noiseGlsl(...names) -> GLSL string with deps first, each once. Throws on an unknown name.

files.usage: const { n2, n3 } = simplex(seed); const field = fbm(n3, 4); value = field(x * 0.01, y * 0.01, t * 0.1). Shader: GL_HEAD + noiseGlsl('fbm', 'ridged') + your main.

exports.name: sdCircle
exports.summary: sdCircle(x, y, r): 2D distance, negative inside.

exports.name: sdBox
exports.summary: sdBox(x, y, hx, hy): exact 2D box distance from half-extents.

exports.name: sdRoundBox
exports.summary: sdRoundBox(x, y, hx, hy, r): 2D box with rounded corners of radius r.

exports.name: sdSegment
exports.summary: sdSegment(x, y, ax, ay, bx, by): distance to a segment.

exports.name: sdCapsule
exports.summary: sdCapsule(x, y, ax, ay, bx, by, r): segment thickened by r.

exports.name: smin
exports.summary: smin(a, b, k): polynomial smooth union, k = blend radius > 0, never above min(a, b).

exports.name: opSmoothSubtraction
exports.summary: opSmoothSubtraction(d, cut, k): smoothly carves cut out of d.

exports.name: rot2
exports.summary: rot2(x, y, a) -> [x, y] rotated counter-clockwise by a radians.

exports.name: opRep
exports.summary: opRep(x, s): repeats a coordinate every s units, centred on 0.

exports.name: opRepPolar
exports.summary: opRepPolar(x, y, n) -> [x, y] folded into one of n angular sectors (radius preserved).

exports.name: SDF_GLSL
exports.summary: GLSL snippets name -> [deps, code]: sdCircle, sdBox2 (2D), sdBox, sdRoundBox, sdSegment, sdCapsule, sdTorus, sdOctahedron (bound), sdGyroid(p, scale, thickness) (bound, pre-scaled 0.6), smin, opSmoothSubtraction, opRep (vec3), opRepPolar (vec2), rot2 (mat2, M * v rotates CCW), calcNormal, calcAO, softShadow(ro, rd, k) (32 steps), march(ro, rd) (64 steps, returns t > 20 on a miss). Raymarch helpers pull in the prototype `float map(vec3 p);` so your map may come after them.

exports.name: sdfGlsl
exports.summary: sdfGlsl(...names) -> GLSL string with deps first, each once. Throws on an unknown name.

files.usage: GL_HEAD + sdfGlsl('sdTorus', 'smin', 'rot2', 'march', 'calcNormal', 'calcAO') + 'float map(vec3 p){...} void main(){...}'. Keep map cheap: SwiftShader pays for every march step. Render at glStart scale 0.5 for raymarched scenes.

exports.name: mtof
exports.summary: mtof(midi) -> Hz (69 -> 440).

exports.name: synthBus
exports.summary: synthBus(ctx, { delay, feedback, wet }) -> { input, analyser, bands() }. Dry + stereo ping-pong delay -> compressor -> tanh limiter (output peak <= 0.87, always) -> analyser -> destination. bands() -> { bass, mid, high, rms } in 0..1 with 50 ms attack / 250 ms release smoothing, so audio-driven visuals do not strobe.

exports.name: fm
exports.summary: fm(ctx, out, t, freq, dur = 0.4, { ratio = 2, index = 3, vol = 0.3 }): FM bell/brass voice with decaying index.

exports.name: sub
exports.summary: sub(ctx, out, t, freq, dur = 0.3, { cutoff = 1800, q = 6, vol = 0.25, type = 'sawtooth' }): subtractive voice, resonant lowpass sweeping down to freq.

exports.name: ksBuffer
exports.summary: ksBuffer(sampleRate, freq, dur, seed, damp = 0.996) -> Float32Array of Karplus-Strong samples (deterministic per seed).

exports.name: pluck
exports.summary: pluck(ctx, out, t, freq, dur = 1, { vol = 0.4, seed = 1, damp }): plucked string from ksBuffer.

exports.name: seq
exports.summary: seq({ bpm = 120, div = 4, seed = 1 }, step) -> play(ctx, out, t0, t1, base). step(ctx, out, time, i, rnd) runs once per step whose offset lies in [t0, t1); rnd is seeded per step, so output never depends on chunking.

exports.name: startSynth
exports.summary: startSynth(play, { target = document, ahead = 0.2, bus }) -> h { ctx, bus, bands() }. Creates the AudioContext only on the first pointerdown/keydown (never autoplays), then schedules play() 0.2 s ahead every 50 ms. bands() is zeros before the gesture. Keep the handle and call h.bands() each frame; do not destructure (const { bands } = startSynth(...)) before the gesture unlocks audio, because the handle's bands is replaced once the bus exists.

exports.name: registerAudioProbe
exports.summary: registerAudioProbe(play, bus) sets window.__demopartyAudioProbe so the Stage 6 OfflineAudioContext probe renders the same play() through the same limited bus from t = 0. Start notes at t = 0 so 2 s clears the RMS floor.

files.usage: const play = seq({ bpm: 92, seed }, (ctx, out, t, i, rnd) => { if (i % 4 === 0) sub(ctx, out, t, mtof(36), 0.4); if (rnd() < 0.4) pluck(ctx, out, t, mtof(60 + (rnd() * 12 | 0)), 1.2, { seed: i }); }); registerAudioProbe(play); const syn = startSynth(play); then each frame: const b = syn.bands(); st.audio = [b.bass, b.mid, b.high, b.rms].

exports.name: GL_HEAD
exports.summary: Fragment header: #version 300 es, highp float/int/sampler2D, uniforms u_time, u_reduced (0 or 1), u_res (px), u_mouse (0..1, y up), u_audio (bass, mid, high, rms), and `out vec4 o`.

exports.name: glProgram
exports.summary: glProgram(gl, frag, vert = fullscreen triangle) -> WebGLProgram. Throws Error with the compile or link log.

exports.name: glSetter
exports.summary: glSetter(gl, prog) -> set(name, number | array) for float, vec2, vec3, vec4, int and sampler2D (pass the texture unit) uniforms; unknown names are ignored. mat*, ivec*, uint* and bool uniforms are unsupported: call gl.uniform* yourself.

exports.name: glDraw
exports.summary: glDraw(gl, fb = null, w, h): binds fb (null = screen), sets the viewport, draws the 3-vertex fullscreen triangle (no buffers).

exports.name: glStart
exports.summary: glStart(canvas, frag, { scale = 1, dprMax = 1, reduce = 0.2, frame }) -> st { kind: 'webgl2', gl, prog, set, time, reduced, mouse, audio, stop }. Prepends GL_HEAD unless frag starts with #version. Resizes to CSS size * min(DPR, dprMax) * scale. Time advances by frame deltas (capped 0.5 s), times `reduce` under prefers-reduced-motion. frame(st) runs before the main draw: do extra passes there and set st.audio.

exports.name: createPingPong
exports.summary: createPingPong(gl, w, h) -> pp { a, b, swap(), w, h, float }, each target { tex, fb }. Read pp.a.tex, glDraw(gl, pp.b.fb, w, h), pp.swap(). RGBA16F when EXT_color_buffer_float exists, else RGBA8; linear filter, repeat wrap. For reaction-diffusion, fluids, feedback trails. glStart sizes the canvas on the first animation frame, so pass a fixed simulation size (e.g. 256, 256) or create the buffers lazily inside frame(st) once gl.canvas has its size.

files.usage: const st = glStart(canvas, noiseGlsl('fbm') + 'void main(){vec2 uv=gl_FragCoord.xy/u_res;o=vec4(vec3(fbm(vec3(uv*4.,u_time*.1))*.5+.5),1);}', { scale: 0.5 }). Canvas CSS should fill the viewport (width:100vw;height:100vh;display:block).

exports.name: gpuStart
exports.summary: async gpuStart(canvas, wgsl, fallback, { scale, dprMax, reduce, storage = 0, workgroups = 0, frame }) -> st { kind: 'webgpu', dev, buf, time, reduced, mouse, audio, stop } or whatever fallback() returns. wgsl defines `@fragment fn fs(@builtin(position) p: vec4f) -> @location(0) vec4f` and reads `u.time, u.reduced, u.res, u.mouse, u.audio`. With storage = n floats and workgroups = w it gets `S: array<f32>` (read_write) and must define `@compute @workgroup_size(..) fn cs(..)`, dispatched w times per frame before the draw. Falls back on no navigator.gpu, no adapter or device, or WGSL validation errors (console.warn, not an error), before touching the canvas, so fallback may reuse it: () => glStart(canvas, glsl). Y axis: WGSL @builtin(position).y points down (0 at the top), while GLSL gl_FragCoord.y and u.mouse.y point up, so port GLSL with p.y = u.res.y - p.y.

files.usage: gpuStart(canvas, WGSL, () => glStart(canvas, GLSL, { scale: 0.5 }), { scale: 0.5 }). The WebGPU path is never gated: the gates serve plain http (no WebGPU), so gates and jury see only the fallback, while https visitors run the WGSL. Prefer WebGL2-only unless the piece needs compute; if you use this, write the WGSL as a faithful port of the GLSL (same motion, same palette, no flashing).

exports.name: oklch
exports.summary: oklch(L 0..1, C 0..~0.37, h degrees) -> sRGB [r, g, b] 0..1. Out-of-gamut colours lose chroma, not hue.

exports.name: hex
exports.summary: hex([r, g, b]) -> '#rrggbb'.

exports.name: cosPal
exports.summary: cosPal(t, a, b, c, d) -> [r, g, b] = a + b * cos(2 pi (c t + d)), Quilez cosine palette.

exports.name: luminance
exports.summary: luminance([r, g, b]) -> WCAG relative luminance.

exports.name: contrast
exports.summary: contrast(x, y) -> WCAG contrast ratio 1..21. Check text and key forms reach 3 or more.

exports.name: ramp
exports.summary: ramp(n, hue, C = 0.12, { L0 = 0.18, L1 = 0.94, hs = 0 }) -> n sRGB colours from dark to light, chroma peaking in the midtones, hue drifting hs degrees (cool shadows to warm lights reads as natural light).

exports.name: GLSL_COSPAL
exports.summary: GLSL vec3 cosPal(float t, vec3 a, vec3 b, vec3 c, vec3 d).

exports.name: GLSL_OKLCH
exports.summary: GLSL vec3 oklch(float L, float C, float hRadians) -> sRGB, clamped (no gamut mapping; keep C under ~0.15).

files.usage: Pick one anchor hue from the brief, build ramp(5, h, 0.1, { hs: 25 }) for the ground and one accent at h + 150 with lower L. Avoid the slop list: no purple-to-blue or teal-to-orange whole-frame gradients, no neon on black by default.

exports.name: clamp01
exports.summary: clamp01(x) to [0, 1].

exports.name: lerp
exports.summary: lerp(a, b, t).

exports.name: smooth
exports.summary: smooth(x): clamped smoothstep 3x^2 - 2x^3.

exports.name: quintic
exports.summary: quintic(x): clamped smootherstep, zero first and second derivative at the ends.

exports.name: cubicInOut
exports.summary: cubicInOut(x): clamped cubic ease in-out.

exports.name: expoOut
exports.summary: expoOut(x): fast start, long settle.

exports.name: backOut
exports.summary: backOut(x, s = 1.70158): overshoots about 10% past 1 then settles.

exports.name: elasticOut
exports.summary: elasticOut(x): springy settle onto 1.

exports.name: beat
exports.summary: beat(t, t0, t1, ease = smooth): eased 0..1 progress through [t0, t1], clamped.

exports.name: CUTS
exports.summary: [0, 5, 10, 15, 20]: the default 4-beat, 20-second storyboard cut times.

exports.name: act
exports.summary: act(t, cuts = CUTS) -> { i: beat 0..3 (held at 3 after the end), p: linear progress 0..1 }.

exports.name: acts
exports.summary: acts(t, cuts = CUTS, blend = 1) -> 4 weights summing to 1, crossfading over blend seconds around each cut. Mix the four beats' parameters with them.

exports.name: storyClock
exports.summary: storyClock({ reduce = 0.2, cuts }) -> (rafMs) => { t, reduced, i, p }. Frame-driven, never loops, 0.5 s delta cap, time times reduce under prefers-reduced-motion. Keep some motion alive after 20 s and make the first frame readable.

files.usage: const clock = storyClock(); requestAnimationFrame(function f(ms) { const { t } = clock(ms); const [w0, w1, w2, w3] = acts(t); scale = w0 * 1 + w1 * 1.4 + w2 * 0.8 + w3 * 1.1; requestAnimationFrame(f); }).
